The Client & The Challenge

'Shanta' is a digital platform designed for undergraduate students in Saudi universities, combining four essential services into a single app: second-hand textbook marketplace, digital notes & summaries bank, student discounts & offers club, and daily student tools (GPA calculator & schedule organizer).

The brand launches with zero prior brand equity (93.3% unaware of predecessors) in a market hindered by low general peer-to-peer trust (3.02/5) and a crowded discount layer dominated by funded incumbents, requiring a targeted entry strategy anchored in academic trust.

Research & Discovery

Target Downloads

50,000 Downloads in Semester 1

Total Budget

SAR 100,000 (across 5 categories)

University Scope

Imam, KSU, and PNU (246K+ Students)

Core Campaign Message

Your Academic Journey: Easier, Cheaper, & Safer

Strategic Alignment (From Research to Strategy)

Go-to-Market decisions were directly calibrated against empirical findings from the Phase 1 market research study:

  1. Positioning Anchored in Academic Trust: Research highlighted low general trust in peer transactions (3.02 / 5), contrasted by high trust in peer ratings (4.18) and ISBN verification (3.89). Consequently, “Shanta” is positioned as a trusted academic exchange platform backed by localized merchant discounts, avoiding direct competition with well-funded generic discount platforms.
  2. Temporary Exclusion of Used Devices: Used hardware ranked lowest in student priorities (2.71), with 20% of respondents raising concerns over feature clutter. Given higher transaction risks, device resale was deferred to Phase 2 to protect early brand equity.
  3. Utilizing Discounts and Notes to Counter Seasonality: Student discounts ranked highest in overall importance (1.98). Integrating seasonal utilities (textbooks) with daily routines (discounts and GPA calculators) ensures continuous engagement and drives Daily Active Users (DAU).

Situation Analysis

1. Brand Identity & Positioning

  • Brand Name: “Shanta” (Arabic for Backpack/Bag) — invoking the daily student essential.
  • Tagline: “Everything a Student Needs.”
  • Positioning Statement: For undergraduate students in Saudi universities seeking savings and transactional security, “Shanta” is the unified digital platform combining verified textbook and note exchanges with student discounts and daily productivity tools, unlike unorganized social media groups that lack trust mechanisms and academic structure.

2. SWOT Matrix

Strengths
  • Four integrated student services consolidated into a single application.
  • Built-in institutional trust mechanisms (Peer ratings 4.18/5, ISBN verification 3.89/5).
  • Verified user accounts authenticated via official university student emails.
  • Near-zero marginal cost for hosting and distributing digital study summaries.
Weaknesses
  • Zero baseline brand awareness (93.3% completely unfamiliar with predecessors).
  • Strong network effect dependency (early utility relies directly on initial inventory volume).
  • New entrant in the student discount space competing with heavily funded incumbents.
Opportunities
  • Highly concentrated metropolitan student population (246,077 undergraduates in Riyadh).
  • Near-universal smartphone adoption (98.4%) and high e-commerce literacy (71%).
  • Substantial textbook price spread (resold at 15% - 50% of original store price).
Threats
  • Unregulated piracy and unstructured PDF sharing across Telegram channels.
  • Depressed baseline interpersonal trust in individual strangers (3.02/5).
  • Entrenched habits using unstructured channels (WhatsApp groups, Haraj).
  • Severe demand seasonality centered around the first three weeks of each semester.

3. Saudi Market Competitor Analysis

Competitor Used Books Digital Notes Student Discounts Daily Tools Market Presence & Scale
Shanta ● ● ● ● Unified ecosystem with verified academic trust
Unipal ○ ○ ● ○ Bahraini-founded discount platform (250K users, 700 brands).
Unicode ○ ○ ● ○ University student discount app (4.8 rating on App Store).
Dawir & Ketapp ● ○ ○ ○ Specialized used book apps with limited activity/updates.
WhatsApp / Telegram Groups ● ● ○ ○ Strong informal competitors; lack security and structure.

Objectives & Target Audience

1. IMC SMART Objectives

  1. Cognitive Objectives: Achieve a minimum of 40% brand and tagline awareness among undergraduates in target universities within the first 60 days.
  2. Affective & Behavioral Objectives:
    • Increase mean declared platform trust from 3.02 / 5 baseline to at least 4.00 / 5 within 90 days.
    • Secure 50,000 app downloads and 30,000 verified student accounts during Semester 1.
    • Generate 10,000 content listings (books & notes) within the first 30 days.
    • Reach 8,000 Daily Active Users (DAU) by the end of Semester 1.
  3. Business & B2B Objectives: Partner with 25 local merchants & cafes adjacent to university campuses prior to ad launch.

2. Audience Segmentation & Buyer Personas

Sara (Undergrad Student)

Primary Segment — Budget-Conscious
Profile: 20 years old, sophomore at Imam University, relies on monthly student stipend (SAR 850 - 1,000).
Motivation: Buying required textbooks and notes at fair prices while tracking her cumulative GPA.
Main Barrier: Fear of transacting with unfamiliar sellers; resolved via mutual ratings and student verification.

Fahad (Tech & Senior Student)

Secondary Segment — Quality & Value
Profile: 22 years old, senior at a private university in Riyadh, higher disposable allowance.
Motivation: Accessing rare specialized foreign references, genuine device offers, and software subscriptions.
Main Barrier: Scarcity of international editions and authenticity concerns; resolved via ISBN edition validation.

Abdullah (Content Creator)

Supply Side — Academic Note Creator
Profile: 21 years old, high-achieving junior student at King Saud University.
Motivation: Monetizing high-quality course summaries and notes for supplemental income.
Main Barrier: Piracy concerns or delayed payouts; resolved via watermarked previews and secure digital distribution.

IMC Strategy

1. Core Campaign Message & Pillars

  • Core Campaign Message: “With Shanta… Your academic journey is easier, cheaper, and safer.”
  • Secondary Tagline: “Your smart shortcut for university life.”

Trust Pillar

"Safer"

Student email verification, bilateral peer ratings, and exact ISBN edition matching.

Ease Pillar

"Easier"

A unified digital hub consolidating book exchanges, study notes, and campus deals in one app.

Value Pillar

"Cheaper"

Fair market pricing without middleman fees, complemented by exclusive on-campus food and supply deals.

2. Media Mix & Channel Allocation

Channels were selected using official Saudi communications data (Internet Saudi Arabia Report):

Channel / Tool Reach Metric Strategic Campaign Role
Snapchat 84.2% Official National Penetration Primary Channel: Broad reach and high behavioral resonance among youth in Riyadh.
TikTok 77.1% Official National Penetration Primary Channel: Engaging short-form video ads, UGC, and campus ambassador showcases.
Twitter / X 46.2% Ad Reach Secondary Channel: Academic discourse, university hashtags, and institutional announcements.
Instagram 49.8% Ad Reach Secondary Channel: Visual showcases of partner deals and student testimonials.
On-Campus Activation Orientation Week Booths Direct Activation: Live demonstrations of ISBN scanning and instant student onboarding.

2. Campaign Timeline (6 Weeks)

The campaign runs from August 9 to September 19, 2026, coordinated with the official start of Semester 1 (August 23, 2026):

Phase Duration Primary Operational Activities
1. Pre-Launch (Teasing) Aug 9 – 22 (2 Weeks) Tech stress testing, ambassador onboarding, closing 25 local campus merchant deals.
2. Official Launch (Grand Opening) Aug 23 – Sep 5 (2 Weeks) High-volume paid ad deployment, Orientation Week campus booths, ambassador content rollout.
3. Retention & Sustaining Sep 6 – 19 (2 Weeks) Shifting message focus toward study notes, GPA tools, personalized push notifications.

  • Role definitions: R = Responsible for execution, A = Accountable / Decision maker, C = Consulted for expertise, I = Informed of progress.

4. Contingency Scenarios

  • Rising TikTok CPI Costs: Dynamically reallocate budget portions to on-campus activations and peer referral incentives.
  • Low Initial Book Inventory: Launch a high-engagement listing raffle with instant rewards for early book listers.
  • Server Performance Bottlenecks: Instantly trigger automated cloud auto-scaling protocols and temporarily pace paid ad bursts.
